business_summary.text: Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Limited (formerly Tata Motors Limited) is an Indian passenger vehicle manufacturer with a portfolio of ICE, CNG and EV models under the Tata brand, and owns Jaguar Land Rover, a UK-based luxury vehicle maker.

call_points.text: Targeting GBP1.7 billion of savings over two years through enterprise cost-out missions to bring breakeven down to 300k units.
JLR FY27 guidance will be shared at the Investor Day on 17 June 2026.
JLR investment spend planned at £18bn over five years from FY24.
JLR targets £1.7bn of cumulative savings over two years from Enterprise Missions.
JLR aims to reduce break-even volumes towards 300k in two years.
JLR Q4 cash balance £2.8bn; total liquidity £6.9bn including undrawn facilities.
Iran conflict impacting fuel prices and consumer confidence.

operating_notes.text: April 2026 total sales stood at 59,701 units, up 31.1% YoY.
FY26 consolidated net debt stood at ₹30.7K Cr after adverse free cash flows the release attributes to JLR production stoppages.
Tata PV FY26 revenue ₹58,465 Cr (+49.4%) with EBITDA margin 9.4%; JLR revenue £6,870 mn, down 11.1%, EBITDA margin 14.0%.
Q4FY26 consolidated free cash flow was ₹11.4K Cr as JLR operations recovered post the cyber incident.
JLR Q4 wholesales 95.3K, up 61.1% QoQ from 59.1K.
Tata PV Q4 EBITDA margin 9.4%, up 150 bps YoY.
JLR total liquidity £6.9bn including £1.7bn undrawn RCF.
Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue reached ~₹105,000 Cr with FCF of ₹11,000 Cr.
May 2026: PV domestic 59,090 units (+42% YoY), PV IB 700 units (+45%), EV domestic+IB 10,517 units (+85%, a new monthly high).
May 2026: VAHAN registrations up 50%+ YoY; company says it is No. 2 in the PV market on registrations.
India PV monthly volume run-rate scaled above 60,000 units from 45,000-50,000 earlier; targeting closer to 70,000.
EV bookings are nearly 3.5x pre-Middle East crisis levels; EV production crossed 15,000 units in July.
JLR VME at 7.1% of sales; Range Rover, Range Rover Sport and Defender now 81% of JLR sales.
